data.narrative:
Black Semiconductor, a Series A chip company founded by Daniel and Sebastian Schall, is evaluated against a comp universe of 11 private peers and 3 public benchmarks in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. Public comparables include ALAB, NVDA, and AMD; leading private peers span SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable to this valuation. The target dataset contains only one same-stage comparable and one adjacent-stage comparable within the Chips & Semiconductors universe—below the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability. An all-sector median approach would introduce substantial noise given the heterogeneity of semiconductor subsegments and company maturity profiles. This constraint reflects the thinly populated early-stage semiconductor financing environment relative to software or consumer tech.

Without a sufficiently dense peer cohort at matching stage and capitalization tier, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range. The €254.4M in total capital raised provides context on historical investor conviction but does not mechanically translate to current enterprise value. Additional methods—such as discounted cash flow modeling (contingent on revenue projections not provided here) or venture capital method analysis (requiring target return assumptions)—would be necessary to establish a defensible range. Key uncertainties include the company's current revenue run rate, gross margins, and the specific technology differentiation relative to the identified peer set.
